candidate.title: RC-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina RC-Seq schematic, resolved as the array-based implementation described by Baillie et al. (2011): genomic DNA fragmentation, capture on retrotransposon-targeted microarrays, paired-end sequencing and reference comparison with known and novel insertion outcomes. RC-seq and retrotransposon capture sequencing are aliases here. The readout carrier is a genomic-DNA-derived sequencing library. Routine library construction and amplification are not decomposed in the drawing. The disconnected left inset, labeled Novel retrotransposition events and RC-Seq: Retrotransposon capture sequencing, illustrates the biological target; it is not linked to Genomic DNA by a material-transfer arrow. The single-cell version mentioned in catalogue prose and enhanced RC-seq in a related abstract are not depicted alternatives or additional targets.

states.label: Genomic DNA
features: Genomic DNA is the substrate; short yellow-green regions are labeled Retrotransposon binding sites.
The biological target is genomic retrotransposon insertion position, represented by retrotransposon sequence associated with flanking genomic DNA.

evidence.rationale: The main input is explicitly labeled Genomic DNA; the green marks above it are labeled Retrotransposon binding sites. The left biological-event inset is separate.

evidence.quote: Retrotransposon capture sequencing (RC-Seq) is a high-throughput protocol to map and study retrotransposon insertions .

Firstly, fragmented genomic DNA was hybridized to custom sequence capture arrays targeting the 5′ and 3′ termini of full-length L1, Alu and SVA retrotransposons (Fig . 1a, Supplementary Table S1, Supplementary Table S2).

states.label: DNA fragments
features: The three blue fragments illustrate a heterogeneous fragment pool; one retains the yellow-green retrotransposon-associated regions.
Informative captured fragments retain a retrotransposon terminus together with linked genomic sequence, enabling insertion-site mapping.

evidence.quote: Lastly, read pairs were mapped using a conservative computational pipeline designed to identify known (Fig. 1c) and novel (Fig. 1d, Supplementary Fig. S1a-d) retrotransposon insertions with uniquely mapped read pairs (“diagnostic reads”) spanning their termini.

states.label: Microarray with transposon binding sites
features: The drawing places the transposon binding sites on a solid microarray surface.

Primary-source clarification of the generic binding-site label: these are oligonucleotide capture probes tiled across the termini of full-length L1, Alu and SVA elements; the paper also includes LTR probes as negative controls.
These targeting sequences define enrichment coverage; the array is a capture reagent, not the sequenced biological analyte.

Capture is imperfect: unwanted genomic fragments can also be retained and sequenced.

operations.label: Fractionate
operations.description: Genomic DNA is broken into shorter DNA fragments, some retaining targeted retrotransposon sequence and adjacent genomic sequence.
operations.mechanism: The primary figure identifies the input fragments as sheared genomic DNA.
operations.information_effect: Shorter DNA molecules retain local sequence relationships where a retrotransposon terminus and its genomic flank remain on the same fragment. The biological insertion predates this preparative transformation.

operations.label: Hybridize
operations.description: Retrotransposon-associated regions of fragmented genomic DNA hybridize to complementary oligonucleotide probes on the microarray. The output retains captured DNA associated with that surface; no separate unbound-material branch is drawn.
operations.mechanism: Sequence-selective hybridization to oligonucleotide capture probes; the reference array implementation targets 5′ and 3′ termini of L1, Alu and SVA.
operations.information_effect: Sequence-dependent enrichment increases representation of targeted retrotransposon termini and linked genomic flanks. It captures both reference and non-reference insertion-bearing molecules; hybridization does not classify them and does not guarantee perfect specificity.

operations.label: Align
operations.description: Use the sequenced-fragment/read-pair information and the depicted reference sequence with Transposon sites to compare insertion contexts. Concordant placement supports known insertions; discordant flank/retrotransposon placement supports candidate novel insertions. Both labeled right-hand outcomes are retained.
operations.mechanism: Primary Figure 1c–d resolves the generic Align cartoon: pairs mapping at a common reference locus indicate known insertions; a uniquely placed genomic end paired with an end mapping to a distal retrotransposon indicates a candidate non-reference insertion. The paper calls such nonconcordant mates unpaired; they originate from paired-end sequencing.
operations.information_effect: Produces insertion-site and reference-status evidence from sequence associations. Unique informative mapping is required for localization. The two outcomes are data classifications, not a physical split or separate preparations; additional evidence is needed to establish somatic origin.

method_scopes.rationale: All four operation instances apply to RC-Seq at the declared schematic scope. The image name expands to retrotransposon capture sequencing, and the verified collection heading and caption identify the same RC-seq array workflow. Baillie et al. describes this implementation. The collection mentions scRC-seq separately; Upton describes a distinct single-cell/LNA-probe implementation and Shukla reports enhanced RC-seq. Neither is an explicitly depicted alternative in this image. This assignment does not imply that all RC-seq family implementations use this array preparation.
